hero.headline: Do You Really Know What Your Business Is *Worth* — and What That Makes Possible?
hero.subhead: For US business owners 52–67 running a $3M–$10M company: get a defendable valuation and a clear view of how that value fits your whole financial picture — so you can grow it, borrow against it, reward key people, plan retirement, transition to family, or one day sell, all from a position of knowledge instead of guesswork.

problem.title: Most Owners Can't Confidently Answer One Question: *What's It Worth?*

items.title: Your Number Is Fuzzy
items.body: Without a real valuation, every major move — borrowing, investing, hiring, rewarding a key employee, transitioning, or selling — is a guess.

items.title: No One Connects the Dots
items.body: You have a CPA, attorney, banker, and financial advisor, but nobody ties your business value to your personal financial picture and goals.

items.title: Untapped Leverage
items.body: Your company is likely your largest asset — yet without clarity you can't fully use it for financing, growth capital, retirement income, or legacy.

problem.transition: Knowing your number isn't just for selling — it's the *foundation for every confident financial decision* you make.

faqs.q: Do I have to be planning to sell?
faqs.a: Not at all. A valuation is for clarity first — it tells you what you've built and what it makes possible: growth, financing, rewarding key people, retirement income, family transition, or a future sale. Selling is just one option among many.

faqs.q: I already have advisors — why do I need this?
faqs.a: Most owners do. The issue isn't whether you have people; it's whether anyone is connecting your business value to your personal financial picture, with one accountable plan.

faqs.q: How can knowing my value help me right now?
faqs.a: A defendable number strengthens financing and lending conversations, informs whether to grow or hold, guides how you reward and retain key people, and makes your personal retirement and estate planning real instead of theoretical.

faqs.q: I'm too busy for a big project.
faqs.a: That's exactly why we work in 90-day sprints — small, high-impact moves that create clarity and leverage instead of adding chaos.

faqs.q: Is this a pitch for a financial product?
faqs.a: No. We start with a clarity call and assessments to establish your number and your options. Any strategy is built around your business, taxes, and family — never a cookie-cutter product.

faqs.q: What does the clarity call cost?
faqs.a: The initial Business Value & Clarity Call is complimentary, with no obligation.
